payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear definition and explanation of second-order co-occurrence matrices, detailing their construction and application in measuring semantic relatedness.

claims.text: A second-order co-occurrence matrix is constructed from a first-order co-occurrence matrix and represents the average of first-order co-occurrence vectors associated with terms.
Second-order co-occurrence vectors measure the relatedness of terms based on the frequencies of other words that co-occur with both terms, rather than their direct co-occurrence frequencies.
Incorporating semantic similarity into second-order co-occurrence matrices improves the correlation with human judgments of similarity and relatedness.
